gen-nixie-one-gf-exo-2: Exo 2 is a clean sans with plenty of daylight inside every curve, so it recedes without fuss. Nixie One's constant, nostalgic stroke from top to baseline is the real hook.
gen-nixie-one-gf-fustat: Fustat bends like tubing, with a wide gap where the c ends. Nixie One's retro display stroke stays constant from top to baseline, which is the pair's most memorable trait.
gen-nixie-one-gf-gothic-a1: Retro-tech and nostalgic, Nixie One draws each stroke like a stout pipe cleaner up top. And Gothic A1 steps in beneath, plain sans with a splayed c terminal and an approachable manner.
gen-nixie-one-gf-host-grotesk: Retro-tech and nostalgic, Nixie One traces a consistently thick outline with open curves. Host Grotesk sweeps its curves open beneath it, a contemporary sans-serif that lets the display lettering lead.
gen-nixie-one-gf-ibm-plex-sans-hebrew: Nixie One draws every letter with one uninterrupted line width. IBM Plex Sans Hebrew sits underneath with uncrowded mouths on its s and c, giving the display lettering room.
gen-nixie-one-gf-ibm-plex-sans-jp: Nostalgic Nixie One gives its round letters walls that match the straight strokes, with open curves and clear gaps. IBM Plex Sans JP then reads approachably, curve after curve ending open.
gen-nixie-one-gf-ibm-plex-sans-kr: Retro-tech lines, traced at the width of a single stylus: that's Nixie One. IBM Plex Sans KR would carry paragraph after paragraph smoothly with a modern openness at every curve end.
gen-nixie-one-gf-k2d: Nixie One is nostalgic, retro-tech lettering with open curves. It earns its keep big and short, while K2D, a clean sans-serif with tube-like strokes and far-hanging c terminals, handles the rest.
gen-nixie-one-gf-kanchenjunga: Kanchenjunga holds its shape at low resolution, like a technical drafting pen. Make Nixie One small, or Kanchenjunga large, and the display font's open, nostalgic curves lose their room.
gen-nixie-one-gf-kumbh-sans: A constant stroke from top to baseline defines Nixie One. It handles the nostalgic flourish, while Kumbh Sans, a sans-serif with terminals cut well short of the bowl, carries the steady talking.
